test: make orphan inherit-rejection getdata checks able to fail

PeerTxRelayer.assert_never_requested compares the hash of every request
received, an int, with its argument, and test_orphan_inherit_rejection
passed it hex strings. An int never equals a str, so these checks passed
whatever the node requested. Pass ints instead.

Two more changes let the checks see the requests they are about:

- Relay the parent from peer2 rather than peer1. Relaying it made the
  node request it from peer1, so the check that peer1 never requested
  the parent fails once it compares ints.
- Bump mocktime by TXREQUEST_TIME_SKIP before the peer1 and peer2
  checks. The node requests an orphan's missing parent after a delay,
  so without the bump the request has not been sent when they run.

Also correct the comment on why the parent is rejected: it exceeds the
maximum standard weight, and the node rejects it with tx-size.

To check each assertion can fail, the scenario was mutated in a scratch
copy so that the node does request the hash, and each call site was
evaluated with both the old and the new argument. The old one passed
every time, and the new one failed:
- parent not relayed: peer1 is asked for the parent, peer2 for the
  child's txid;
- child not relayed: peer2 is asked for the child's txid;
- child relayed from peer2: peer2 is asked for the child's wtxid;
- neither child nor grandchild relayed: peer3 is asked for the child's
  txid.
Without the mocktime bumps, the first two mutations pass with ints too.

test: look for the wtxid in p2p_blocksonly

The connection that checks a transaction submitted over RPC is not
announced to a block-relay-only peer uses P2PTxInvStore, which negotiates
wtxidrelay. The node would therefore announce the transaction by its
wtxid, and the assertion looked for the txid, which cannot be in the
store for a transaction carrying a witness: it passed whether or not the
transaction was announced.

Assert on the wtxid instead. With the connection opened as
outbound-full-relay rather than block-relay-only, the old assertion still
passes and the new one fails.

Also open an outbound-full-relay connection and assert that the wtxid
was announced on it. The two assertions differ only by `not`, so if the
announcement or its id changes, the test fails instead of the absence
check passing silently.

gui: wallet: Use v0 PSBT

PSBTv2 is not very interesting for current GUI users, and defaulting to
it causes issues for existing users. To make this change minimal and
avoid touching strings, this commit, only changes the default back
instead of making the version configurable.

The external signer PSBT will still be version 2, and I've added an
explicit argument here to show that. This will break users who are using
HWI versions < 2.1.0.
(https://github.com/bitcoin-core/HWI/releases/tag/2.1.0)

memusage: Make fields of STL helper structs public

The `stl_tree_node`, `list_node` and `unordered_node` class templates
only mimic the layout of the standard library's container nodes, so
that `sizeof` yields an estimate of the memory they use. Their fields
are never accessed.

Since llvm/llvm-project#237374, Clang 24 diagnoses these fields with
`-Wunused-private-field`.

This change drops the `private:` access specifiers. It does not affect
the size or alignment of the structs, as all their fields keep the same
access control, and it is consistent with `stl_shared_counter`.

author Eugene Siegel <elzeigel@gmail.com> 1794855165 -0500
committer fanquake <fanquake@gmail.com> 1795003020 +0000

net_processing: set fDisconnect instead of calling DisconnectNode

MaybeDiscourageAndDisconnect calls DisconnectNode which creates a
CSubNet containing only the CNode's address. This will disconnect
every CNode with the same IP address. This is normally not a problem,
except for clearnet-over-tor. If a node has an honest clearnet-over-tor
inbound connection, the IP of the inbound peer will be the exit node's
IP address. If an attacker connects to the node through the same exit
node and sends an invalid message, they can cause every inbound peer
sharing the exit node's IP to get disconnect. Fix this by only
disconnecting the misbehaving CNode rather than every CNode sharing
the IP.
